facts.statement: Wukongopterus is a basal pterosaur genus discovered in the Tiaojishan Formation of Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: Wukongopterus is a genus of basal pterosaur, found in Liaoning, China, from the Tiaojishan Formation, of the Middle or Late Jurassic.

facts.statement: The genus was described and named in 2009 by Wang Xiaolin, Alexander Kellner, Jiang Shunxing, and Meng Xi.
facts.quote: The genus was described and named in 2009 by Wang Xiaolin, Alexander Kellner, Jiang Shunxing and Meng Xi.

facts.statement: The specific name honors Li Yutong, a senior preparator at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology.
facts.quote: The specific name honours Li Yutong, senior preparator of the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology (IVPP).

facts.statement: Evidence suggests the type individual broke its shin while alive.
facts.quote: The type individual appears to have broken its shin during life.

facts.statement: The estimated wingspan of this species is 730 mm.
facts.quote: Its wingspan is estimated at 730 mm.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Wukongopterus may have possessed an uropatagium, a membrane between its hind legs.
facts.quote: Wukongopterus also may have had an uropatagium, a membrane between the hind legs.

facts.statement: Wukongopterus is classified within the family Wukongopteridae.
Wukongopterus lived between 168.2 and 152.21 million years ago during the Bathonian to Kimmeridgian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Bathonian to Kimmeridgian (168.2 to 152.21 million years ago)

rejected.statement: This pterosaur was unusual for possessing both an elongated neck and a long tail.
rejected.quote: It was unusual for having both an elongated neck and a long tail.
